title: Backcasting Robust Mechanistic Explanations: Stress-Testing a Causal-Scrubbing Hypothesis Under Distribution Shift

original_idea.body:
# Backcasting Robust Mechanistic Explanations: Stress-Testing a Causal-Scrubbing Hypothesis Under Distribution Shift

**Problem:** Success state (ARC): formal mechanistic explanations that flag anomalous behavior on novel inputs. Causal scrubbing validates a circuit hypothesis on the training distribution, but the safety payoff is anomaly detection on OOD inputs. The untested gap: does a hypothesis that passes causal scrubbing in-distribution still hold (low scrubbed-loss increase) under mild distribution shift?

**Direction:** Take a published small-model circuit (e.g., the IOI or induction-head circuit in GPT-2 small) and a documented causal-scrubbing hypothesis. Re-run the scrubbing on shifted input distributions (different templates, lengths, content) and measure how the recovered-loss metric degrades. Existing open code (TransformerLens) and a single GPU.

**Why it matters:** Working backward from explanation-based anomaly detection, the explanation must be stable off-distribution. Measuring scrubbing-metric decay under shift tells us whether mechanistic explanations are a sound foundation for the ARC anomaly-detection vision — using only public circuits and open tooling.

**Relevant context:** Causal Scrubbing (Alignment Forum, Redwood); ARC anomaly-detection-via-explanation agenda; IOI/induction-head circuits public in TransformerLens. Causal scrubbing is the most permissive in the abstraction-strictness hierarchy.
